item.title: Parcel volumes grew again in February
item.description: Carriers handled 4 percent more parcels than a year earlier, an industry group said.
item.content:encoded:
Rates on the busiest lanes were flat against December.

Analysts said Amazon moved a growing share of its own volume in the quarter.

item.title: Database licensing shifts toward subscriptions
item.description: Buyers said perpetual licenses now account for less than a third of new spending.
item.content:encoded:
Resellers said Oracle moved most renewals onto subscription terms last year.

Analysts said Oracle had traded upfront revenue for a steadier stream.

One buyer said Oracle audits had become less frequent.

Support pricing at Oracle rose 4 percent, the resellers said.

item.title: Grocery pricing pressure is squeezing margins
item.description: Supermarket chains cut list prices on staples for a second quarter running.
item.content:encoded:
Suppliers said Target had pushed hardest on private-label pricing this year.

Analysts said Target would protect trips rather than basket size.

One supplier said Target asked for longer payment terms.

Shelf space at Target for national brands narrowed again, suppliers said.

Reporting by the newsroom; editing by the standards desk.

item.title: Wire Two | Insect numbers are rebounding, an Amazon basin survey finds
item.description: Ecologists said larvae counts in the basin rose for a second season after years of decline.
item.content:encoded:
Caterpillar species tracked by the survey recovered fastest in protected habitat.

Deforestation in the Amazon basin slowed 8 percent, the survey said.

Shell fragments of river molluscs were counted along the same riverbank.

Conservation groups said the canopy is still thinner than in 2015.

Reporting by the newsroom; editing by the standards desk.

item.title: Amazon adds two fulfillment centers in the Midwest
item.description: Amazon.com, Inc. ($AMZN) said the two sites will add 1,800 jobs and open before the holiday season.
item.content:encoded:
The investment totals $450 million across the two facilities.

Hiring for the first site begins in April, the company said.

item.title: Advertisers test new privacy tools
item.description: Agencies said the new measurement tools reduce reported conversions by about a tenth.
item.content:encoded:
Buyers said Meta shipped its version to large advertisers in January.

Two agencies said Meta had absorbed the measurement loss in its own reporting.

A rival said Meta still holds the largest share of social budgets.

Spending with Meta rose 4 percent in the quarter, one agency said.

item.title: Federal agencies push cloud consolidation
item.description: A memo directs agencies to cut the number of separate hosting contracts by a third within two years.
item.content:encoded:
Procurement officers said the timetable is ambitious but not impossible.

$ORCL is one of four vendors on the existing schedule.

item.title: Wire Two | Across the valley, Apple growers brace for frost
item.description: Growers said an early frost damaged blossom across the valley and the harvest may fall by a fifth.
item.content:encoded:
Growers said Apple futures on the produce exchange rose 6 percent as buyers weighed a smaller crop.

Caterpillar damage in the same orchards was lighter than last season.

Reporting by the newsroom; editing by the standards desk.

item.title: University endowment posts a 7 percent return
item.description: The fund now stands at 3.4 billion dollars after distributions.
item.content:encoded:
The endowment office said in a statement that the portfolio returned 7 percent for the year, ahead of its policy benchmark by about a point.

It said private holdings were marked down while public equities carried the result.

The treasurer said the spending rate would stay at 4.5 percent for the coming year.

item.title: Wire Two | Cloud spending growth cooled in the quarter
item.description: Enterprise buyers slowed new commitments while renegotiating existing contracts, two resellers said.
item.content:encoded:
Resellers said Amazon still won most of the largest renewals in the quarter.

Analysts said Amazon had held pricing steady while rivals discounted.

One buyer said Amazon offered longer terms rather than lower rates.

Growth at Amazon in that segment remains above the market average, analysts said.

Reporting by the newsroom; editing by the standards desk.

item.title: CAT scan backlogs ease at the imaging clinic
item.description: Waiting times for imaging fell by a fifth after two clinics extended hours.
item.content:encoded:
Radiology staff said the backlog built up during the winter.

A Meta-analysis of scan volumes found the same pattern in three regions.

Patients now wait about nine days for a scan.

item.title: Meta Platforms fined over ad tracking by the Irish regulator
item.description: Meta Platforms, Inc. (NASDAQ: META) was fined 210 million euros by the Irish regulator, which said advertisers' data had been processed without a lawful basis.
item.content:encoded:
The company said it would appeal the decision.

The regulator gave it six months to change its consent flow.

item.title: Wire Two | New inscriptions found at the Oracle of Delphi site
item.description: Archaeologists said the inscriptions name two temple officials and a treasurer.
item.content:encoded:
One inscription names the Apple of discord, the myth that opens the Trojan war.

Reporting by the newsroom; editing by the standards desk.

item.title: Wire Two | Upgrade cycles for smartphones keep lengthening
item.description: Two carriers said the average replacement cycle has passed four years in their largest markets.
item.content:encoded:
Carriers said Apple has stretched that cycle furthest, trimming quarterly sales of new handsets.

Analysts at two firms said Apple would offset the slowdown with services revenue.

One supplier said Apple accounted for a fifth of its shipments last year.

Rivals have not matched Apple on trade pricing, the carriers said.

Reporting by the newsroom; editing by the standards desk.

item.title: Oracle wins a federal database contract
item.description: Oracle Corporation (NYSE: ORCL) won a five-year federal contract to consolidate agency database systems.
item.content:encoded:
The award is worth up to $600 million.

Work begins in the third quarter, the agency said.

item.title: Wire Two | Rival vehicles gain access to charging networks
item.description: Three operators said cross-brand access will be available at most sites by the summer.
item.content:encoded:
Operators said Tesla had opened the largest share of its connectors so far.

Analysts said Tesla earns a margin on every session sold to other brands.

One operator said Tesla hardware needed only a firmware change.

Drivers using Tesla connectors pay a small premium, the operators said.

Reporting by the newsroom; editing by the standards desk.

item.title: Wire Two | A slow-burning thriller, anchored by Ford
item.description: The actor plays a retired pilot in a film that runs two hours and ten minutes.
item.content:encoded:
The film reunites him with the director of Oracle, a thriller from 2019.

Ford has not appeared in a cinema release since 2023, critics noted.

Reporting by the newsroom; editing by the standards desk.

item.title: Transit line clears its final vote
item.description: Opponents said the eastern route would displace two blocks of small workshops.
item.content:encoded:
The authority said in a statement that the line will open in phases from 2029, with the first two stations serving the eastern district.

It said the cost estimate has not changed since the last review, and that federal funding covers about a third of the total.

A spokesperson said crews would begin work on the tunnel section in June.

item.title: Meta-analysis finds statin benefit overstated
item.description: The systematic review pooled 42 randomized trials and found a smaller effect on cardiac events than earlier estimates.
item.content:encoded:
Patients in the placebo groups had similar cholesterol readings at baseline.

Patients had CAT scans at baseline in 14 of the pooled trials.

The authors said the journal will publish the full cohort data in June.
